key_insight: CARS anchors attention to coronary centerlines to predict pressure and velocity on patient-derived lumen geometries, reducing geometry-fusion cost from O(N²) to O(N n_f).
engineering_relevance: The surrogate delivers coronary flow predictions in 87 ms per case versus 572–1,063 s for CFD, enabling rapid pressure-based assessments.
method: Inputs: image-derived centerline, per-point lumen radius, and scalar inlet flow rate.
Uses each case’s centerline as the attention focal set to predict fields at arbitrary query points.
Trains territory-specific models on steady incompressible Navier–Stokes solutions from OpenFOAM.
evidence_signal: Trained on 2,700 solutions per territory, CARS achieved pressure/velocity relative ℓ₂ errors of 0.120/0.149 (left) and 0.063/0.119 (right), with 97.7%/96.3% agreement on the CFD-derived FFR ≤ 0.8 decision.
watch_item: Predicted velocity is insufficiently continuity-consistent for derived quantities, and model weights are territory-specific.
paper_title: CARS: a centerline-anchored attention surrogate for coronary blood flow on skeleton-generated lumen geometries
